newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland to set international bond in 1997 - finmin.
newsitem.headline: Poland to set international bond in 1997 - finmin.

text.p: Finance Minister Marek Belka said on Wedensday Poland's 1997 international bond issue will mainly aim to highlight the country's standing to make it easier for corporate borrowers to tap international capital markets.

"We will be present on the capital markets (in 1997) simply to provide a point of reference, a benchmark, for other potential participants of the capital market," Belka said at his first news conference since he took office early this month.
"Without continuous verification of our financial standing on the international markets, it is harder for non-governmental entities to participate in the markets," he added.
He declined to unveil the size, timing or the lead manager of the planned issue.

The 1997 budget allows the government to borrow up to $500 million in the international markets, and finance ministry officials said earlier they are eyeing the U.S and Japanse markets for the issue after placing Eurobonds in 1996 and 1995.
Poland returned to the international capital market two years ago after striking a crucial debt restructuring deal with foreign commercial banks.
Poland's sovereign debt currently has a B-minus Standard & Poor's rating, Baa3 from Moody's Investors Service and BBB from IBCA.
